sources.entry: poethepoet - A task runner that defines tasks in pyproject.toml and works with poetry or uv.

summary.one_liner: Poe the Poet is a task runner that defines project tasks in pyproject.toml (or poe_tasks.toml) and runs them inside poetry's or uv's virtualenv.
summary.what_it_does: Tasks are declared under [tool.poe.tasks] as plain commands, shell scripts, Python expressions, or references to Python functions. Extra CLI arguments are appended to the underlying command when a task is run. Tasks can declare named CLI arguments with defaults that can reference environment variables, and can be composed to run in sequence, in parallel, or as a DAG. Running poe with no arguments lists the tasks, grouped and with optional help text. The README also mentions .env file support, shell completion for task names and arguments, and use as a poetry plugin, standalone CLI, or embedded library.
use_cases: replace a Makefile for Python project commands
run test, lint, or serve tasks in a poetry or uv project
define named CLI arguments for project scripts
run tasks in sequence or in parallel
load environment variables from .env files for scripts
notable: Works inside poetry or uv virtualenvs without needing poetry run or uv run
Tasks can be Python function references, not only shell commands
Tasks can be defined in shared Python packages for reuse
Ships an official Agent Skill for AI coding agents
caveats: Automatic virtualenv handling is described for poetry or uv projects; other setups use a specified env
The shell task type is described as posix-only in the README example
